events.title: Apollo 11 Lands Humans on the Moon
events.description: The lunar module Eagle touched down in the Sea of Tranquility, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to land on the Moon. Armstrong stepped onto the surface hours later, just after the landing had been completed in the evening in U.S. time (late on July 20 in the U.S. and into July 21 in UTC).
events.significance: It fulfilled President Kennedy's goal of landing a human on the Moon and returning safely, and it stands as one of the great achievements in human exploration.

events.title: The July 20 Plot Against Hitler
events.description: Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg planted a bomb in Adolf Hitler's headquarters, the Wolf's Lair in East Prussia. Hitler survived with minor injuries, and the attempted coup that was meant to follow collapsed within hours. Stauffenberg and other conspirators were executed that night and in the following weeks.
events.significance: It was the best-known attempt by German officers to overthrow the Nazi regime from within, and it has become a lasting symbol of German resistance.

events.title: Viking 1 Lands on Mars
events.description: NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down on the Martian surface at Chryse Planitia. It went on to send back the first clear images from the surface of Mars and to carry out experiments searching for signs of life.
events.significance: It was the first successful U.S. landing on Mars and gave scientists their first detailed look at the planet's surface.

events.title: Birth of Sir Edmund Hillary's Fellow Explorer Is Not Included; Instead: Birth of Sir Edmund Hillary
events.description: Edmund Hillary was born in Auckland, New Zealand, on July 20, 1919. He grew up to become a beekeeper and mountaineer.
events.significance: In 1953, he and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
